Budget: 350 CAD, per-day
Appetite for effort: gentle

Would rule the trip out: Nothing that needs to be at a place before 09:00, No guided group tours

Pace: slow
Interests: Roman archaeology, Baroque painting, markets
In their words: We have been to Rome once, thirty years ago, and saw the obvious things then. We would rather spend a whole morning in one place than see four.

candidates.title: Morning at Mercato di Testaccio
candidates.summary: A covered, flat-floored neighbourhood market with food stalls where you can graze slowly on Roman street food, a market rather than a monument. The party gave no dietary restrictions, so none are accounted for. Check opening days before going.

candidates.title: Lunch at Flavio al Velavevodetto
candidates.summary: A Roman trattoria built into the side of Monte Testaccio, an ancient hill of discarded amphorae, so lunch comes with archaeology visible through glass. Access to the dining rooms and any steps there has not been checked.

candidates.title: Dinner at Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina
candidates.summary: A deli and restaurant known for cured meats, cheeses and carbonara, a long, unhurried dinner. The streets nearby are cobbled, so a taxi to the door may be kinder. Some seating may involve stairs, which is unverified. Dietary needs are not accounted for.

candidates.title: Pizza bianca at Antico Forno Roscioli
candidates.summary: A historic bakery for pizza bianca and Roman pastries, a short stop rather than a meal. It is a standing-room counter with little seating, and the surrounding lanes are cobbled.

candidates.title: Browse Mercato Trionfale
candidates.summary: One of Rome's largest covered markets, near the Vatican, with fresh produce, cheese and cured meat. It is a quieter, local alternative to the tourist markets and pairs naturally with a Vatican-area morning. Opening days are not checked.

candidates.title: An afternoon gelateria
candidates.summary: A kind of place rather than a named one: a seated gelateria for an unhurried afternoon pause between galleries. Pick one with chairs on a smooth street. Dietary needs were not stated.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel in Prati, near the Vatican Museums
candidatesAccepted.summary: Prati has flat, wide, mostly paved streets rather than cobbles, and it is close to the Vatican collections for unhurried mornings. Ask for a room reached by lift with handrails. No map listing of specific hotels was supplied, so this is a kind of place, not a named property. The nightly band is an estimate and would take a large share of a 350 CAD daily budget.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel in Monti, near the Forum and Colosseum
candidatesAccepted.summary: Monti puts the Roman archaeology (the Forum, the Palatine and Trajan's Markets) within a short walk or taxi ride. Its own lanes are cobbled and sloped, so choose a hotel on a main street such as Via Cavour, with a lift. This is a kind of place, not a named premises. The price band is an estimate for October.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Piazza del Popolo or Via del Corso
candidatesAccepted.summary: This base is central for Baroque painting: Caravaggio in Santa Maria del Popolo and San Luigi dei Francesi, and the Galleria Borghese nearby. The main streets here are flatter, but side streets are cobbled. Confirm a lift and step-free access before booking. This is a kind of place only, and the price band is an estimate that may exceed what the daily budget comfortably allows.

candidatesAccepted.title: Palazzo Massimo alle Terme (National Roman Museum)
candidatesAccepted.summary: Superb Roman frescoes, mosaics and sculpture in a calm, lift-equipped museum near Termini, well suited to a slow morning in one place. Step-free access details should be confirmed with the museum.

candidatesAccepted.title: Galleria Borghese
candidatesAccepted.summary: Caravaggio and Bernini in a compact villa; timed entry keeps it uncrowded. Entry requires advance booking. The walk through the park to reach it may be long, so a taxi to the door is wise.

candidatesAccepted.title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
candidatesAccepted.summary: A private princely collection with Caravaggio and Velázquez's Innocent X, quiet and unhurried. Lift availability should be checked in advance.

candidatesAccepted.title: Palazzo Barberini (Gallerie Nazionali)
candidatesAccepted.summary: Caravaggio, Raphael's La Fornarina and Pietro da Cortona's vast Baroque ceiling fresco. Lifts reportedly available, though this should be confirmed.

candidatesAccepted.title: Centrale Montemartini
candidatesAccepted.summary: Classical sculpture displayed among old power-station machinery, rarely crowded and largely flat. Access details are unverified.

candidatesAccepted.title: Capitoline Museums
candidatesAccepted.summary: The Marcus Aurelius bronze, the Capitoline Wolf, and Caravaggio's Fortune Teller, plus views over the Forum without walking it. The piazza approach includes ramps and cobbles; use the side access.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mercato Testaccio
candidatesAccepted.summary: A covered, flat, modern food market with produce stalls and lunch counters, easier underfoot than Campo de' Fiori. It is closed on Sundays.

candidatesAccepted.title: San Luigi dei Francesi and Sant'Agostino Caravaggios
candidatesAccepted.summary: Free churches holding Caravaggio's Matthew cycle and Madonna of Loreto. They are close together, but the streets between them are cobbled. Opening hours were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Check ETIAS requirement for Canadian passport holders
candidatesAccepted.summary: Canadians visiting the Schengen area are expected to need ETIAS travel authorisation once it is in operation; confirm the current status and validity rules with official EU sources well before departure. Passport validity rules for Schengen entry are also worth checking. This is not clearance to travel.

candidatesAccepted.title: Travel medical insurance for travellers aged 68 and 71
candidatesAccepted.summary: Ontario provincial coverage abroad is very limited, and premiums and pre-existing-condition clauses vary sharply with age, so compare policies with trip-cancellation and emergency medical cover. I could not account for health history, which drives price.

candidatesAccepted.title: Timed-entry tickets for Galleria Borghese
candidatesAccepted.summary: Borghese entry is by timed reservation and sells out, which suits a long unhurried visit to Caravaggio and Bernini without a group tour. Choose a slot after 09:00. Lift access exists, but confirm step-free routes with the museum.

candidatesAccepted.title: eSIM or roaming plan for Italy
candidatesAccepted.summary: A data plan lets you call taxis through apps and check step-free routes, which avoids long cobbled walks. Compare a Canadian carrier's roaming plan with a prepaid European eSIM, and check phone compatibility.

candidatesAccepted.title: Palazzo Massimo alle Terme (National Roman Museum)
candidatesAccepted.summary: Roman archaeology at a slower pace than the Forum: the frescoes from Livia's villa and the bronze boxer, indoors on level floors near Termini. Lifts are reported, but we could not confirm them for every floor, so check access before going. Band assumes standard adult tickets in CAD. Over-65 concessions for non-EU visitors may not apply.

candidatesAccepted.title: Galleria Borghese
candidatesAccepted.summary: Caravaggio and Bernini in one compact villa, made for spending a whole unhurried visit in one place. Entry is by timed reservation, and slots can sell out weeks ahead. The band assumes the standard ticket plus the booking fee. The garden paths around the villa are gravel, and we could not account for how far the walk is from the nearest drop-off.

candidatesAccepted.title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
candidatesAccepted.summary: A private princely collection with Caravaggio and Velázquez's portrait of Innocent X, quieter than the big museums. The band assumes the standard ticket with the audio guide included. We could not verify how step-free the gallery is. It is just off Via del Corso, which is paved rather than cobbled.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mercato Testaccio
candidatesAccepted.summary: A covered, modern market on flat floors in a residential district, good for slow browsing and a casual lunch. The band covers food and snacks for two, not shopping. We could not check opening days for October 2027.
